steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Media doesn't just report events — it constructs them through selection, framing, and emphasis, shaping how audiences understand social issues. | Key Fact: Agenda setting: the media doesn't tell people what to think, but it tells them what to think about. By choosing which stories to cover, media sets the public agenda. | Key Fact: Framing: how a story is presented (the angle, language, images) shapes its meaning. The same event can be framed as a 'protest' or a 'riot', a 'freedom fighter' or a 'terrorist'. | Key Fact: Moral panics (Stanley Cohen): when the media defines a group or behaviour as a threat to social values, creating public fear and demanding action. E.g. mods and rockers, video nasties, knife crime.
